name: Eduyot — Testimonial Format of Halakhic Transmission
notes: The unique format of Tractate Eduyot whereby rulings are transmitted as formal testimonies (eduyot) before sages; the halakhic and jurisprudential significance of this mode of transmission

name: Recording Minority Opinions in Halakha
notes: The principle and rationale for recording dissenting individual opinions alongside the majority ruling, so future courts may rely on them; discussed explicitly in Eduyot 1:5-1:6

name: Disputes of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
notes: The body of halakhic disputes between the schools of Shammai and Hillel, including cases where Beit Shammai is lenient and Beit Hillel strict, and vice versa; their practice of intermarrying despite disputes

name: Beit Hillel Changed Their Opinion to Follow Beit Shammai
hebrew: חזרו בית הלל להורות כדברי בית שמאי
notes: The specific instances recorded in Eduyot where Beit Hillel reversed their position and ruled according to Beit Shammai's opinion

name: Court Overruling a Prior Court's Decision
hebrew: בית דין מבטל דברי בית דין חברו
notes: The rule that a court may not overturn another court's ruling unless it exceeds the prior court in both wisdom and number; Eduyot 1:5

name: Impurity of a Limb Severed from a Living Person
notes: Dispute among Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Joshua, and Rabbi Nehunia regarding the impurity status of flesh and bone severed from a living person (as opposed to a corpse); Eduyot 6:2-6:3

name: Drawn Water Invalidating a Mikveh (Mayim She'uvim)
notes: The quantity of drawn water that invalidates a mikveh; dispute between Shammai (nine kavs), Hillel (a hin), and the testimony of weavers in the name of Shemaiah and Avtalion (three logs); Eduyot 1:3

name: Minimum Measure of Dough for Challah Obligation
notes: Dispute between Shammai (one kav), Hillel (two kavs), and the Sages (kav and a half / five quarters) regarding the minimum measure of dough obligated in challah; Eduyot 1:2

name: Redemption of Firstborn Donkey That Died Before Redemption
notes: Dispute whether the owner bears financial responsibility if the firstborn donkey dies before redemption; Eduyot 7:1

name: Oven Cut Into Rings (Tannur) — Susceptibility to Impurity
notes: Testimony that an oven cut into rings with sand between them is susceptible to impurity; Rabbi Eliezer disagrees; Eduyot 7:7 (related to the famous Tannur shel Akhnai context)

name: Conditional Intercalation of the Year
notes: Testimony that a year may be intercalated conditionally, pending approval by a leader; case of Rabban Gamliel who approved upon return from Syria; Eduyot 7:7

name: Intercalation Throughout the Entire Month of Adar
notes: Testimony that the year may be intercalated throughout all of Adar, not only until Purim; Eduyot 7:7

name: Elijah's Role in Restoring Disputed Lineage
notes: The tradition that Elijah will come to clarify genealogical disputes — removing those wrongly admitted and admitting those wrongly excluded; debate among Rabbi Joshua, Rabbi Judah, Rabbi Shimon, and the Sages; Eduyot 8:7

name: First Sanctification of Jerusalem — Permanent for All Time
hebrew: קידוש ראשון קידש לשעתו ולעתיד לבוא
notes: Rabbi Joshua's testimony that the original sanctification of Jerusalem sanctified it for its own time and for the future, permitting sacrifices even without the Temple standing; Eduyot 8:6

name: Offering Sacrifices Without the Temple Standing
notes: Rabbi Joshua's view that sacrifices may be offered even without the Temple, and most holy sacrifices eaten without the curtains; Eduyot 8:6

name: Akavia ben Mahalalel — Refusal to Retract and Excommunication
notes: The story of Akavia ben Mahalalel who refused to retract four rulings despite being offered the role of head of court; his excommunication and death while excommunicated; Eduyot 5:6-5:7

name: Deaf-Mute Woman's Marriage and Divorce
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Nehunia ben Gudgada that a deaf-mute woman given in marriage by her father can be divorced with a get; Eduyot 7:9

name: Stolen Beam Built Into a Palace — Monetary Restitution
hebrew: קורה גזולה שבנאה בבירה — תשלום דמים
notes: Testimony that a stolen beam built into a palace may be restored through monetary payment of its value rather than returning the beam itself; Eduyot 7:9 (related to the Talmudic principle of takkanat hashavim)

name: Sin Offering Stolen When Theft Was Unknown — Atonement Valid
hebrew: חטאת גזולה שלא נודע לרבים — כיפר
notes: Testimony that a stolen sin-offering whose theft was not publicly known still effects atonement for the welfare of the altar; Eduyot 7:9

name: Half-Slave Half-Free Person (Chatzi Eved Chatzi Ben Chorin)
notes: The status and obligations of a person who is half-slave and half-free; Beit Shammai's argument that the master must emancipate him to allow him to fulfill the obligation of procreation; Beit Hillel changed their ruling; Eduyot 1:13

name: Retroactive Reckoning of Niddah Impurity
notes: Dispute between Shammai, Hillel, and the Sages about how far back a woman's niddah impurity applies retroactively upon discovery; the 24-hour rule vs. the examination-to-examination rule; Eduyot 1:1

name: Exchanging Second Tithe for Uncoined Metal
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Dosa and the Sages whether second tithe may be redeemed for uncoined metal (asimon); Eduyot 3:2

name: Fourth Year Vineyard — Laws of Fifth and Removal
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether fourth-year vineyard fruit is subject to the additional fifth (chomesh) and the law of removal (biur); Eduyot 4:5

name: Minimum Value for Valid Kiddushin (Perutah vs. Denar)
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (a denar or its value) and Beit Hillel (a perutah or its value) as the minimum for valid betrothal; Eduyot 4:7

name: Old Get (Get Yashan) — Seclusion After Writing
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding whether a get written before the husband secluded himself with his wife again is still valid; Eduyot 4:7

name: Rival Wives (Tzarot) and Yibbum Eligibility
notes: Major dispute between Beit Shammai (permits rival wives to the surviving brothers for yibbum) and Beit Hillel (forbids); consequences for priestly fitness after chalitzah or yibbum; Eduyot 4:8

name: Purity of Liquids in the Temple Slaughterhouse
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer that liquids in the Temple slaughterhouse are pure (not subject to impurity); Eduyot 8:4

name: Purity of the Ayal Locust
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer (Yose the Permitter) that the ayal locust is pure/permitted; Eduyot 8:4

name: Impurity from Touching a Corpse (Testimony of Yose ben Yoezer)
hebrew: טומאת מגע במת — עדות יוסי בן יועזר
notes: Yose ben Yoezer's testimony that one who touches a corpse becomes impure (he declared this as a leniency relative to the prior practice); Eduyot 8:4

name: Validity of Get/Document — Depends on Signatories
hebrew: גט שכתבה היא ושובר שכתבו הוא — כשר
notes: Testimony that a document's legal validity depends only on its signatories, not on who physically wrote it; a wife may write her own get and a husband may write his own receipt; Eduyot 2:3

name: Proselyte Who Converted on Erev Pesach — May He Bring Korban Pesach
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (may immerse and eat the Passover sacrifice that evening) and Beit Hillel (compared to one separating from a grave, must wait); Eduyot 5:2

name: Whether Kohelet Defiles the Hands (Canonical Status)
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (Kohelet does not defile the hands) and Beit Hillel (it does defile the hands), regarding the canonical/sacred status of Ecclesiastes; Eduyot 5:3

name: Placing Fowl on a Table with Cheese
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (fowl may be placed on the same table as cheese but not eaten together) and Beit Hillel (may neither be placed nor eaten together); Eduyot 5:2

name: Nazirite Who Made Vow Outside the Land and Came to Israel
hebrew: נזיר שגלח בחוץ לארץ ובא לארץ
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about how long such a nazir must observe naziriteship upon arriving in the Land of Israel; Eduyot 4:11

name: Nazirite — Two Witness Groups Testifying Different Numbers of Neziruyot
hebrew: נזיר שיש לו שתי כתות עדים
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (testimony divided, no naziriteship) and Beit Hillel (two are included within five, must be nazirite twice) when witnesses disagree on the number of neziruyot vowed; Eduyot 4:11

name: Large Forgotten Sheaf — Whether Subject to Shikchah
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (a four-kav sheaf that was forgotten is not subject to shikchah) and Beit Hillel (it is subject); Eduyot 4:3-4:4

name: Declaring Ownerless for the Poor Only
notes: Dispute whether declaring produce ownerless only for the poor (but not for the rich) counts as valid hefker for peah/shikchah purposes; Beit Shammai permits, Beit Hillel requires hefker for all; Eduyot 4:3

name: Offspring of a Peace-Offering — May It Be Brought as a Peace-Offering
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Joshua and Rabbi Papias that the offspring of a peace-offering may itself be brought as a peace-offering; Rabbi Eliezer disagrees; Eduyot 7:6

name: Morning Tamid Offered at the Fourth Hour
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Judah ben Bava that the morning daily offering was brought at the fourth hour; Eduyot 6:1

name: Wine Forty Days Old as Valid for Altar Libation
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Judah ben Bava that wine forty days old was used as a libation on the altar; Eduyot 6:1

name: Female Captive and Her Eligibility to Eat Terumah
notes: Dispute regarding a priest's wife taken captive: whether she may eat terumah upon return; the role of self-testimony and corroborating witnesses; Eduyot 3:6

name: Family of Doubtful Lineage (Issa)
notes: Status of a family of doubtful lineage (issa) and whether widows from such families may marry kohanim; the authority of courts to investigate such lineage; Eduyot 8:3

name: Pigeon Racers Disqualified as Witnesses
notes: Testimony that those who fly racing pigeons are disqualified from giving testimony; Eduyot 2:7

name: Doubtful Tumah in Public vs. Private Domain
hebrew: ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים ורשות היחיד
notes: Cases of doubtful impurity debated between Rabbi Joshua (impure) and the Sages (pure) involving impure person passing pure person, and impurity in public vs. private domains; Eduyot 3:7

name: Ashes of Red Heifer Defiled by Touching Part of Them
notes: Testimony of Rabbi Shimon ben Bathyra that if a defiled person touched part of the ashes of purification, the whole batch is defiled; Eduyot 8:1
